title: Does the 'probe beats judge' advantage hold once the input is adversarially paraphrased?

original_idea.body: Reproduce a probe-vs-judge comparison, apply meaning-preserving paraphrases/perturbations, and measure the robustness gap to see whether the probe's lead survives; one open model.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: testing whether the probe-beats-judge lead survives paraphrase informs reliance on internal monitoring (level 4).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Probe-vs-judge reproduction + paraphrase perturbation on one open model; guided (level 4).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped with clear success criterion (robustness gap under paraphrase) (level 5).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public model, curated paraphrases, externally runnable stress test (level 4).

low_compute.reasoning: Probe + judge inference, no training; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Probe-vs-judge and paraphrase robustness studied; combination partly open; partially addressed.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Paraphrase stress-test combination may be partly open.
